plain.text: Paul came to Derbe and Lystra, where a disciple named Timothy lived; his mother was a Jewish believer and his father was Greek. The believers spoke well of him. Paul wanted Timothy to come along, and had him circumcised because of the Jews in that area, who knew his father was Greek. As they travelled, they delivered the Jerusalem decisions, and the churches were strengthened in faith and grew daily.

Paul and his companions were kept by the Holy Spirit from preaching in the province of Asia, and the Spirit of Jesus would not allow them to enter Bithynia. At Troas, Paul had a vision in the night of a man of Macedonia begging him, "Come over to Macedonia and help us." They concluded God had called them to preach the gospel there. (Here the writer begins to say "we", suggesting he joined the journey.)

They sailed to Philippi, a Roman colony and leading city of Macedonia. On the Sabbath they went outside the city gate to the river, expecting a place of prayer, and spoke to the women gathered there. One was Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth who worshipped God. The Lord opened her heart to respond to Paul's message. She and her household were baptised, and she persuaded them to stay at her home.

A slave girl who had a spirit of fortune-telling earned a lot of money for her owners. She followed Paul for many days, shouting, "These men are servants of the Most High God." Finally Paul, troubled, said to the spirit, "In the name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her!" It left her. Her owners, realising their hope of making money was gone, dragged Paul and Silas before the magistrates, accusing them of causing an uproar. The crowd joined the attack. They were stripped, beaten with rods, thrown into prison, and their feet fastened in stocks.

About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening. Suddenly a violent earthquake shook the prison; the doors flew open and everyone's chains came loose. The jailer woke, saw the doors open, and drew his sword to kill himself, thinking the prisoners had escaped. Paul shouted, "Don't harm yourself! We are all here!" The jailer rushed in trembling and asked, "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?" They replied, "Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household." They spoke the word of the Lord to him and all in his house. He washed their wounds, and immediately he and all his household were baptised. He brought them into his house, set a meal before them, and was filled with joy because he had come to believe in God, along with his whole household.

In the morning the magistrates sent word to release them. But Paul said, "They beat us publicly without a trial, even though we are Roman citizens, and threw us into prison. Now do they want to get rid of us quietly? No! Let them come themselves and escort us out." The magistrates were alarmed to hear they were Roman citizens. They came, apologised, and asked them to leave the city. After visiting Lydia's house and encouraging the believers, they left.

summary.bigIdea: The good news reaches Europe: Lydia believes, a girl is set free, and a jailer and his household come to faith.
points: The Spirit guides Paul to Macedonia through a vision.
Lydia, a businesswoman, believes and welcomes them into her home.
Beaten and jailed, Paul and Silas sing at midnight, and the jailer asks, "What must I do to be saved?"
summary.reflection: Paul and Silas sang in prison at midnight. What helps you praise God when things are dark?
